exposure: types of NU interventions received (e.g., phototherapy, IV antibiotics, thermal/fluid support, oxygen, tube feeds, transfusions)
management setting (NU vs. Special Baby Ward)
feeding practices (IV fluids vs. formula during separation)
outcome: proportion of babies receiving no neonatal unit interventions
cohort: 2978 inborn newborns admitted to Neonatal Units (NUs) or the Special Baby Ward (SBW) across two hospitals in Ghana (Greater Accra Regional Hospital and Tamale Teaching Hospital) between January and December 2022.
finding: The study found that 11.5% of inborn newborns admitted to Neonatal Units received no intensive interventions, and administering IV fluids instead of formula during separation was associated with significantly higher exclusive breastfeeding rates at discharge.
